newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK says Japan to extend generous visa treatment.
newsitem.headline: HK says Japan to extend generous visa treatment.

text.p: Japan has agreed to accord future Hong Kong passport holders the same visa treatment as holders of Hong Kong British travel documents, the government said in a statement on Thursday.
The territory will start issuing Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (SAR) passports after it reverts to China at midnight of June 30.

About three million of Hong Kong's 6.4 million people hold some type of limited British travel document. These include the British National Oversees (BNO) passport, which grants no residency rights in Britian but offers some consular protection.
An estimated 750,000 hold passports of countries such as Canada, Australia and the United States, while the rest hold only a travel document that confers no nationality.
A Hong Kong government spokesman said the government intended to maintain its treatment of Japanese visitors, who are allowed to enter Hong Kong without a visa for up to one month.
Hong Kong has been lobbying nations around the world to give generous treatment to SAR passport holders.
The United States last month said it would grant SAR passport holders the same visa treatment now enjoyed by holders of Hong Kong British travel documents.
